gap: No result ChatGPT got states Notebookcheck's chest-strap numbers side by side: Benedikt Winkel measured the Apple Watch Series 11 at 0.4% average heart-rate deviation (max 2 bpm) against a Polar H10, versus 5.2% (max 9 bpm) for the Galaxy Watch8 44 mm LTE and 2.37% (max 7 bpm) for the Watch8 Classic, with measured battery of about 36 h (Series 11, no workouts) vs about 24 h (Watch8 with always-on display).
standout_why: Tech Advisor (cited, opened 2026-11-10) gives no heart-rate, GPS or step figures for any pick and quotes battery as maker claims except the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2. Android Authority and WIRED (cited) returned 403 / blocked and could not be read; neither is a lab and their roundups in the result list are editor picks, not strap-referenced measurements. Tom's Guide's 5,000-step Apple Watch 11 vs Venu 4 piece is in the results (uncited) but its body could not be retrieved, so its numbers are not on any page ChatGPT showed the shopper. The Notebookcheck deviation and runtime figures are new and useful but do not fully decide the pick because the Garmin Venu 4 has no lab figure I could open.
decides: Confirms the Apple Watch Series 11 (ChatGPT's 'Series 12' card is not a product on any page opened) as the pick for iPhone users who care about heart-rate accuracy: 0.4% average deviation and max 2 bpm off a Polar H10 is the tightest figure among the candidates, and Notebookcheck's 36 h measured runtime beats Apple's own 24 h claim. It weakens the Galaxy Watch8 for serious workout HR: 5.2% average and a 9 bpm miss in the same lab's protocol, and roughly 24 h of measured battery with always-on display. The Venu 4's battery and HR advantages remain maker-claim-only on this page set; TechRadar's 30-minute run numbers (strap 156 bpm vs Venu 4 151 bpm) exist but the page could not be opened and are listed as unsourced.
